## Research record — PydanticAIRunner lifecycle revalidation (ticket c465)

**Conclusion: no restructuring of `run()`'s ownership is warranted right now.** The existing
ADR 0056/0058 decomposition already gives every effect/resource concern in `run()` a single,
correct owner. This pass's evidence, and the one gap it found and closed with a
characterization test, follow.

### 1. Effect/resource boundary timeline (AC1)

Walked `PydanticAIRunner.run()` (runner.py:371-758, 388 lines) end to end and named every
boundary, its owner, and its required ordering:

1. Event-loop displacement guard -> `drive_off_event_loop` (runner_support.py)
2. Extras/import guard -> `_import_pydantic_ai()`
3. Config/preflight -> `_effective_config`, `_pai_check_config`
4. Tracing setup -> `setup_tracing` (best-effort, no-op on failure)
5. Tool/toolset assembly (agentic vs single_turn) -> `assert_gated` FAIL-CLOSED, runs BEFORE
   any provider client is built (runner.py:261, tested: test_provider_session_guard.py
   `test_the_gate_refusal_runs_before_any_provider_client_is_built`)
6. Model resolution -> `_pai_model`, `_recover_slot_endpoint` (model_classes.py)
7. Provider/session construction -> `with ProviderSession(cfg) as provider_session:`
   (providers.py) — owns the provider client lifecycle end to end (entered/exited via the
   `with` statement itself; ADR 0056 decision 2, story a49e)
8. Fallback/model-scope build -> `build_fallback_model` / `infer_model` (model_classes.py);
   `model_scope = ExitStack()` owns the wrapper's OWN lifecycle, disjoint from
   ProviderSession's set (a provider handed a client never adopts it)
9. Tool-capability check -> `_check_tool_capability`, per fallback candidate
10. Capability/cache/web settings -> `capabilities_for`/`cache_settings_for`/`provenance_for`/
    `web_search_capabilities` (capabilities.py)
11. Model settings + usage limits -> `build_model_settings`/`build_usage_limits` (agent_call.py)
12. Agent kwargs assembly -> `build_agent_kwargs`/`apply_structured_seams` (agent_call.py)
13. Agent execution -> `agent.run_sync` (text) or `_pai_structured` (structured), inside
    try/except/finally
14. Failure accounting (except Exception) -> `usage_log.record_failure`,
    `step_failures.record`, then `interpret_failure(...)` (agent_call.py, ADR 0056 decision 3)
    — ALWAYS RAISES, so nothing after this executes on the failure path
15. Resource teardown (finally) -> `model_scope.close()` first (closes what pydantic-ai's
    fallback wrapper owns), then `ProviderSession.__exit__` fires on the outer `with`'s own
    exit (closes what rebar's builders opened) — order is deliberate and tested
    (test_provider_session_guard.py `test_a_successful_run_closes_the_session_exactly_once`,
    `test_the_session_is_driven_through_the_context_manager_protocol`)
16. Answer attribution -> `_answering_model`, OUTSIDE the ProviderSession `with` block
17. Pre-finalization logging -> `log_call_success` (agent_call.py) — deliberately BEFORE
    finalize_outcome, by design (its own docstring), so the record survives a subsequent raise
18. Finalization -> `_findings.finalize_outcome` — **OUTSIDE both the ProviderSession
    `with` block and the failure-accounting try/except** (see gap below)
19. Run-shape/spend recording -> `_merge_success_run_shape`, `record_call_spend`
    (agent_call.py) — also outside both guards
20. Return `result`

### 2. Consumer census — semantic vs. text/string (AC2)

- **Semantic** (Serena `find_referencing_symbols` on `PydanticAIRunner.run`): 46 test files
  plus exactly one non-test production caller, `docs/experiments/f6fc_live_memo_nudge.py` (an
  experiment script, not a runtime path). All production runtime callers go through
  `get_runner()`'s registry dispatch, confirmed separately.
- **String/dynamic** (grep for `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_mod, ...)` /
  `monkeypatch.setattr(runner_module, ...)`): ~25 distinct targets across
  test_llm_timeouts.py, test_rp01_s5_authoritative_oracle.py, test_llm_fallback_chain.py,
  test_agent_build_invariants.py, test_llm_provider_factory.py, test_pydantic_ai_runner.py,
  test_provider_session_guard.py, test_rp04_s5_decision_auth_heldout.py,
  test_code_review_usage_attribution.py, test_settings_builders_seam.py,
  test_completion_wrapper_duration_instrumentation.py, test_web_tool_gating.py,
  test_agentic_message_cache.py, test_eval.py, test_execution_mode_dispatch.py — targets
  include `_import_pydantic_ai`, `_pai_structured`, `capabilities_for`, `_pai_model`,
  `ProviderSession`, `build_usage_limits`, `get_runner`, `_pai_check_config`,
  `primary_endpoint_for`, `cache_settings_for`, `_local_proxy_bypass_base_url`.
- **`grep -rln 'get_runner\|RUNNERS\[\|runner.run('` under `src/rebar`** found 30 production
  files depending on the `run()` entry point (code_review/, plan_review/, workflow/, evals/,
  operations.py, failure.py, enrich.py, spec_scan.py, epic_bug_screen.py, review_bot/adapter.py,
  and one `_engine/rebar_reconciler` site).
- **Agreement**: semantic and string censuses agree — every monkeypatch target found by grep
  is a name genuinely imported into `runner.py`'s module namespace (many carry an explicit
  `# noqa: F401 (re-exported for tests / back-compat)` comment already documenting this), so
  there is no discrepancy to explain. No compatibility-re-export hazard was found that isn't
  already flagged in source.

### 3. Fault matrix (AC3)

Most of the raising-boundary matrix this ticket asks for **already exists** from a prior pass
(story a49e / ADR 0056 decision 2): `tests/unit/test_provider_session_guard.py` characterizes
a raise in the provider-session pre-call window (the historical leak this ticket's sibling
work fixed), the gate-refusal-before-construction ordering, and transport-close-swallows-raise.
`tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py` characterizes fallback-entry raises (an error in the
fallback condition selects the fallback; an error outside it propagates without failover; every
chain client is closed exactly once by the one session).

**One boundary was NOT yet characterized: a raise during finalization.** `finalize_outcome`
(runner.py:725) runs strictly after BOTH the `ProviderSession` `with` block has exited (its
sibling statement at :708 sits at the same indent as the `with` at :452) AND the
failure-accounting try/except has closed (the `finally` at :702-707). Confirmed by observation
(not inspection): a raise there propagates raw out of `run()`, and:
- `log_call_success` (:716) already fired — BY DESIGN, per its own docstring, so this is
  correctly NOT a gap.
- `record_call_spend` (:751) — runs AFTER finalize_outcome, so a raise there means **no spend
  row is written for a call that burned real tokens**. This is the mirror case to bug 8455
  (which covers a raise during the agent call itself, inside the except block, where
  `usage_log.record_failure` now covers it) — but 8455's fix does NOT cover this later boundary.
  `interpret_failure`/`step_failures.record` are likewise skipped, since they're also inside
  the closed try/except.

Added `test_a_raise_in_finalize_outcome_still_logs_but_skips_the_spend_row`
(tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py) to characterize this as CURRENT, observed behavior —
proven RED-capable by a source mutation (moved `log_call_success` after `finalize_outcome`,
confirmed the log-fired assertion goes red for the right reason) then restored GREEN. No OS
sandbox was needed for the mutation check since it only reordered two logging/dict-building
statements — no filesystem-deletion code was ever in the perturbed path.

### 4. Selected design (AC4)

**No module/class/function gains responsibility and no code is deleted.** The census confirms
every extracted concern (settings/usage builders, Agent kwargs, success logging, spend
recording, provider-session guard, failure interpretation) already has exactly one owner in
`agent_call.py`/`providers.py`/`model_classes.py`/`structured_run.py`/`runner_support.py`.
`run()`'s remaining 388 lines are the orchestration sequence itself — the one thing that
CANNOT be extracted without becoming exactly the generic hook/plugin bus this ticket forbids,
since sequencing five/six owned helpers in a fixed, effect-and-resource-dependent order is
irreducibly what an orchestrator does. No second session owner, no generic lifecycle framework
is proposed.

### 5. Provenance/settings honesty (AC5)

Provenance (`provider_provenance` dict) and `ran_model` are mutated post-construction — e.g.
`provider_provenance["ran_model"] = ran_model` at runner.py:709 happens AFTER the fallback
chain has run and the ANSWERING model is known, which cannot be known at construction time.
Model settings, by contrast, are built once (`build_model_settings`) and passed into the Agent
kwargs unmutated thereafter. No frozen/immutable carrier is proposed for either — that would be
decorative given the call graph genuinely mutates provenance post-construction, which is
exactly the trap this ticket names.

### 6. Size/ratchet discipline (AC6)

All six in-scope files are within the 800-LOC hard cap with headroom: runner.py 785,
agent_call.py 435, structured_run.py 602, providers.py 344, model_classes.py 595,
runner_support.py 153 (2914 total). Complexity: `ruff check --select C901` flags `run()` at 23
and `_memo_toolsets` at 16 (both over the 15-per-branch threshold), but
`python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` confirms both are ALREADY baselined at
their current values (`active=39 new=0 increased=0 stale=10`) — my test-only change didn't
touch source, so nothing changed. `run()`'s complexity is inherent orchestration glue over
already-owned helpers, already tracked by the project's own shrink-only ratchet, not a fixable
defect this ticket should chase. No function-NLOC ratchet, per-file headroom assertion, or new
size threshold is proposed — this paragraph is an advisory debt signal only, per Testing.

### 7. ADR disposition (AC7)

**No ADR amendment is needed.** ADR 0056 already authorizes exactly this seam structure
(decisions 1-4: extract `interpret_failure`, settings/usage builders, Agent kwargs +
success logging + spend recording, and the provider-session guard) and ADR 0058 already made
the 800-LOC module cap the sole governing size ceiling (removing per-file headroom assertions
this ticket's constraints also forbid re-adding). This research found nothing that changes
either accepted decision. The one unanswered assumption this pass surfaces going forward: the
finalize_outcome-raise spend-row gap (section 3) is real product behavior worth a deliberate
decision (fix vs. accept), but fixing it is OUT OF SCOPE for this research ticket per its own
"must not repeat prior extraction" framing — filing a follow-up ticket rather than expanding
scope here (see below).

### Outcome & disposition

**(a) Research-only.** This ticket closes on the research record above plus the one
characterization test added (tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py); no production code
changed. `make lint`, `make typecheck` are clean; the full local suite
(`make test`) shows 18057 passed / 10 failed / 63 skipped, and the 10 failures are confirmed
PRE-EXISTING and unrelated (reproduce identically with this ticket's one test-file change
`git stash`ed out — atomic_completion_close, rebar_repo_isolation, tracker_footprint_cli,
api_surface_gate; none touch the llm/ subsystem).

**Filed as a follow-up** (not fixed in this ticket's scope): the finalize_outcome-raise
spend-row gap from section 3 — a real, if narrow, billing-accuracy gap. Will be created as a
`discovered_from`-linked ticket before this one closes.
